info.title: Anyroute API
info.description: Scope: a documented subset of the public HTTP API that the Anyroute router implements. It covers the model catalog, chat completions, embeddings, key creation and listing, generations, status, health and receipts, plus the blind-token issuer keys and purchase (present only when the router enables blind tokens) the Oblivious HTTP gateway keys, gateway and relay list (present only when the router enables Oblivious HTTP) the transparency log of keys and configurations with its tiles, checkpoints and witness cosignatures (present only when the router enables it) the Lane: model variants, day-zero candidates and creator royalty claims, Private RAG (answers from documents sent with the question, nothing kept), and the Batch API (many chat or embeddings requests run in the background at a discount, with the lines and answers kept sealed outside the database until the results expire). It also covers teams as anonymous organisations: roles, passkey and wallet members, org budgets and the hash-chained audit log with its export, and characters: Tavern cards called as @character/<id>, with a memory ledger encrypted on the client. Other implemented routes (for example legacy completions, the /v1 aliases, key updates, credits, Stock Token payments, BYOK, wallet sign-in, rankings, provider onboarding and the paymaster) are not described here, and a route's absence from this document does not mean it is absent from the router. Endpoint availability, payment modes and model capabilities are deployment-specific. Errors share the OpenRouter-shaped ApiError body; the 4xx responses each operation can return are declared with the reusable responses in components.responses.

tags.description: Unlinkable paid access with Privacy Pass tokens (RFC 9578 type 0x0002, blind RSA per RFC 9474). Present only when the router enables blind tokens.

tags.description: Oblivious HTTP gateway (RFC 9458) and the relays that reach it, behind the unlinkable lane. Present only when the router enables Oblivious HTTP.

tags.description: What each provider has documented about how it handles a prompt (retention, jurisdiction, legal hold, training use), and the request options that route on it.

tags.description: Claim a model's creator royalty by publishing a challenge in the Hugging Face repository the weights come from.

tags.name: Responses
tags.description: OpenAI Responses API compatible endpoint for the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Codex CLI and other Responses clients. Stateless: nothing is stored.

tags.name: Private RAG
tags.description: Answers from documents sent with the question, ranked in memory and kept nowhere, through the router's own embeddings and chat routes.

tags.name: Transparency log
tags.description: An append-only log (C2SP tlog-tiles, RFC 6962 hashing) of the keys and configurations clients encrypt to or verify against: receipt keys, Oblivious HTTP key configurations, blind-token issuer keys, measurement bundles and sidecar key bindings. Checkpoints are signed notes (C2SP tlog-checkpoint) that witnesses cosign (C2SP tlog-cosignature, cosignature/v1). With TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED, each new checkpoint is also recorded in Sigstore's Rekor log (a hashedrekord entry signed with an ECDSA P-256 anchoring key), an alternative to witnesses. Present only when the router enables it (TLOG_ENABLED).

tags.name: Ollama
tags.description: The Ollama API under /ollama for Ollama clients (Open WebUI, Continue, the ollama libraries, LangChain's ChatOllama): set the client's host to <router>/ollama. Chat, generate and embed calls run on the same keys, lanes and signed receipts as chat completions; the key is sent as Authorization: Bearer.

tags.name: Batches
tags.description: The Batch API: many chat completions or embeddings requests sent in one call and run in the background on the router's worker, at 50% of the normal price, with results kept for 24 hours after the batch finishes.

tags.name: Rerank
tags.description: Rerank documents against a query (Cohere and Jina shape), billed per token or per search unit, with a signed receipt.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: Anonymous organisations: an owner that is an account, a wallet or a Safe (EIP-1271), members who join by passkey or wallet, roles (owner, admin, dev, viewer, agent), an org budget, and a hash-chained audit log you can export and verify offline.

tags.name: Status page
tags.description: The public status page: availability, latency and error budgets per privacy lane and API surface, and incidents with Atom and RSS feeds. The public lane is summed from request outcomes; the attested and unlinkable lanes come only from the differentially private hourly releases at /api/v1/stats (source: dp-noised).

tags.name: Characters
tags.description: Tavern character cards (V2 and V3, as JSON or PNG) called as model @character/<id>: public, unlisted or private (encrypted on the client), with a chat endpoint that defaults to the attested lane, group turn order and creator attribution (counts and cost only).

tags.name: Memory
tags.description: A memory ledger for characters, encrypted on the client: the router stores ciphertext under a scope it cannot link to a character, and embeddings only when the caller opts in.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: Secured Skills Hub for agent skills (a folder with SKILL.md and its scripts and resources): import from a git repository or an archive, a static scan for data exfiltration, prompt injection, obfuscation, dangerous shell commands, untrusted package indexes and binaries, a sha256 content hash of a canonical tar, gated downloads and paid installs (90% to the author, 10% network fee) with a signed receipt. Scanned, not guaranteed.

post.summary: Apply or re-apply a network host using existing wallet authentication
post.description: Available only with NETWORK_HOSTS_ENABLED=true; default false. See /docs/#network-host-signup. Policy offer terms enable shadow offers during probation; signup does not activate payouts. Scheduled renewal checks the current signed policy without promoting hosts to live. Failed attestation blocks selection; policy refusal rejects the host and disables offers. Admission records attested retention with the policy version and leaves jurisdiction, legal hold and training use undeclared; rejection clears the disclosure profile.

get.description: Available only with HOST_DASHBOARD_ENABLED=true (default false). Reuses existing attestation, measurements, proof-time and host-root records. Hardware evidence and recorded measurements do not establish build admission approval, source equivalence or prompt handling. Uses existing walletAuth five-minute validity and replay protection. The recovered wallet must equal providers.operator, case-insensitively. This signature authorizes no payment.

get.summary: List public live models

parameters.name: lane
parameters.description: public (default) lists every live model. attested lists only models with at least one endpoint served under attested retention with a fresh attestation right now. unlinkable lists the same models where the router serves that lane, through Oblivious HTTP or over its Tor onion service (otherwise 501).

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: Comma-separated variants to keep: mainstream, native_low_refusal, abliterated. A restricted variant (native_low_refusal, abliterated) is listed only while an attested provider whose attestation reports the in-enclave classifier serves it, and only such endpoints are counted for it.

parameters.name: output_modalities
parameters.description: Comma-separated output modalities to keep (text, embeddings, rerank, ...); a model is kept when it outputs any of them. all, or unset, keeps every model.

post.description: Supports standard JSON responses and Server-Sent Events when stream is true. A model must support requested capabilities such as tools or response_format. Auth may use a bearer key, wallet authentication, or the per-call payment flow. A 402 response can contain a quote; follow its payment instructions before retrying the exact request. When the router has x402 enabled, the 402 body is also an x402 v1 payment requirement (x402Version, accepts): sign the exact-scheme USDG authorization and retry with X-PAYMENT; the paid response carries X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Two opt-in modes run several billed calls for one request and are off unless the router enables them: model anyroute/council (a panel of models plus a judge; see the council field) and verify "dual" (the same request to two providers; see the verification field). Both are non-streaming only. Where the router enables blind tokens, Authorization: PrivateToken token=<base64url> pays with one token instead of a key (see the Blind tokens tag): the call is charged to a pooled account, the signed receipt carries the token's nullifier and no payer, and the token is spent only if the call is served. A token pays for at most its value, so a request whose worst case costs more is refused with 402 token_value_too_low; council mode and verify are refused with 400 blind_unsupported. A refused, unknown, expired or already spent token is a 401 that carries WWW-Authenticate: PrivateToken challenge="...". Disclosure ceilings and lanes apply to token calls exactly as to key calls. Lane unlinkable, where the router enables Oblivious HTTP, is served only for a request that arrives through the gateway (POST /api/v1/ohttp/gateway) by way of an independent relay, paid with a blind token and never a key, and only by attested providers; where the router serves the lane over Tor (data.lanes.unlinkable.via in GET /api/v1/status includes onion), a request that arrives through its onion service (data.onion.url) and is paid with a blind token qualifies in the same way, streamed or not, and a clearnet request cannot claim to have come that way; otherwise it is refused with 403 lane_requires_anonymous_auth for an API key or a wallet (unless provider.lane_downgrade is attested, which serves it on lane attested instead), 403 unlinkable_requires_relay or unlinkable_requires_independent_relay, 401 unlinkable_requires_token with the token challenge when no token is presented, or 503 no_attested_endpoint when no attested endpoint can serve the model. A request that arrives through an independent relay, is paid with a blind token and names no lane is served on lane unlinkable. On lanes attested and unlinkable the router never falls back to an endpoint without a fresh, verified attestation: it answers 503 no_attested_endpoint instead. Within a lane endpoints are weighted uptime x quality x attested_bonus / price^2 (attested_bonus 1.25 on public, 1 elsewhere). On attested and unlinkable the router still terminates TLS and sees the prompt; end-to-end encryption through the router is planned. Through the gateway, streaming needs chunked Oblivious HTTP (message/ohttp-chunked-req), where the router enables it; stream true in a message/ohttp-req is refused with 400 stream_unsupported.

200.description: Completion JSON, or SSE events followed by data: [DONE] when stream is true.

X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Present when an x402 payment was settled for this call: base64 JSON {success, transaction, network, payer}.

schema.description: SSE data events; event data carries JSON chunks.

post.description: Uses a prepaid API key, or no key with the per-call payment flow (HTTP 402, including x402 when enabled). Input may be a string or a non-empty array with at most 2048 items. Where the router enables blind tokens, Authorization: PrivateToken token=<base64url> pays with one token, exactly as for chat completions.

200.description: Embedding response with usage and signed receipt.

post.summary: Create a root key or authenticated sub-key
post.description: Without Authorization, creates an independent root key with an empty balance. With an authorized management or admin key, creates a virtual sub-key under that account. The response includes the new secret once; store it securely. Root-key creation does not fund the key. Never send a secret in a query string.

201.description: New key metadata and one-time key secret.

get.summary: List keys for the authenticated account

200.description: Key metadata for the authenticated account.

get.summary: List generation summaries
get.description: Returns summaries for the authenticated account. The response's next value can be passed as before to request an older page.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned in next. Pass it through without parsing; current versions may return a legacy ISO-8601 timestamp.

200.description: Generation summaries and the next page cursor, if any.

get.summary: Read one generation record
get.description: Returns a full record only to the account owner, the authenticated paying wallet, or (for a call paid with a blind token, which has no account) whoever presents that spent token in Authorization: PrivateToken. The id is supplied as a query parameter because that is the implemented route; do not put API keys or other credentials in URLs.

get.summary: Read public router configuration
get.description: Returns published runtime configuration, chain public fields, job state and catalog counts, and, where the router runs a Tor onion service, its address as data.onion.address (null otherwise). data.lanes reports each privacy lane (public, attested, unlinkable) with available, models and endpoints (how many can serve it right now) and the attested_bonus its selection weight uses; data.lanes.unlinkable.via lists the transports that carry that lane here: ohttp (an independent Oblivious HTTP relay), onion (Tor, through the onion service), both, or none when it is not available. It is not an uptime guarantee.

get.summary: Check process response
get.description: Returns { ok: true } when this process responds. It does not establish dependency health or uptime.

post.description: A v1 receipt (payload, sig, key_id) is checked as before. A v2 receipt is sent as cose (the COSE_Sign1 bytes, base64) and is checked in order: signature, then request_sha256 and response_sha256 when given, then the chunk hash chain when chunks (the data of every streamed event before the receipt, in order) are given, then the anchor path. The result reports each step (signature_valid, hashes_valid, chain_valid, inclusion_valid; null when not run) and valid is false when any step that ran failed.

get.summary: Read a public receipt proof
get.description: Returns the v1 fields unchanged and, when the receipt has one, its v2 encoding in v2 (version is then 2). With format=cose the COSE_Sign1 bytes themselves are returned (application/cose), or as base64 text with encoding=base64; 404 when the receipt has no v2 encoding. The response also carries privacy, the plain-English privacy label computed from the payload (see GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}/privacy); it is added beside the signed fields and is not signed.

200.description: Signed receipt and optional anchor proof.

get.summary: Merkle path to the hourly root
get.description: Public. Once the receipt's hour has been rooted, the OpenZeppelin MerkleProof-compatible path from the receipt's leaf (the v2 leaf when it has one; v=1 selects the v1 leaf, which sits in the same tree) to the root. Before that, rooted is false. anchored is true only when the root was posted to ReceiptAnchor on chain and confirmed; a router without a configured chain keeps the root off chain (status local) and says anchored false.

get.summary: What we saw: the privacy label for one answer
get.description: Public by id, like the receipt itself. A plain-English label computed from the receipt's signed fields: who could read the prompt, who saw the caller's network address, how the call was paid, what the router kept and what hardware answered, in five short lines (summary) and as structured fields (label). The router reads every prompt in memory to route it on every lane, and the label says so. A field the receipt does not carry is reported as not recorded, never assumed; on an unlinkable receipt the address is reported hidden only because that lane is served solely to requests that arrive over Tor (or an independent relay). The label does not verify the receipt: check its signature with POST /api/v1/receipts/verify or the client library, which also computes the same label with privacyLabel(receipt). The same object is returned as `privacy` by GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}, beside the signed payload and never inside it.

get.summary: Merkle path from an enclave receipt to its host root
get.description: Public, where the router runs with HOST_ANCHOR_ENABLED (otherwise the path does not exist). A receipt a provider's sidecar signed with its enclave key, rooted per host: the router collected it from the host's leaf feed, kept it only because its signature verified under the receipt key the host's router-verified attestation binds, and built one Merkle root per host, attestation reference and interval. anchored is true only when that root was posted with ReceiptAnchor.anchorAttested and confirmed (tx, block and anchor_index, the index in ReceiptAnchor.attestedAnchors); a root kept off chain has status local and anchored false. 404 until the leaf has been collected and rooted.

parameters.name: leaf
parameters.description: The receipt's leaf, keccak256(keccak256(canonical payload || signature)), as 0x and 64 hex characters.

200.description: The host root that holds the leaf, the path to it, and its anchor status.

post.summary: Merkle path for a sidecar receipt, by receipt or leaf
post.description: Public, where the router runs with HOST_ANCHOR_ENABLED (otherwise the path does not exist). A receipt a provider's sidecar signed with its enclave key, rooted per host: the router collected it from the host's leaf feed, kept it only because its signature verified under the receipt key the host's router-verified attestation binds, and built one Merkle root per host, attestation reference and interval. anchored is true only when that root was posted with ReceiptAnchor.anchorAttested and confirmed (tx, block and anchor_index, the index in ReceiptAnchor.attestedAnchors); a root kept off chain has status local and anchored false. 404 until the leaf has been collected and rooted. With receipt, the leaf is recomputed from its payload and signature, and a leaf the receipt states must match it.

receipt.description: The sidecar's receipt envelope as it was delivered.

sig.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of payload.

200.description: The host root that holds the leaf, the path to it, and its anchor status.

get.summary: The router's receipt signing keys
get.description: Every Ed25519 key the router has signed receipts with, current and retired, as a JWKS. A receipt is checked by canonicalizing its payload (keys sorted, no whitespace), verifying the signature with the key whose kid is the receipt's key_id, and confirming the kid is the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the raw key. The same list is served at /api/v1/receipts/keys.

get.summary: What the router has verified about a provider's attestation
get.description: Public. status is attested only while the router holds a fresh attestation it verified itself, simulated only for development evidence outside production, and unverified otherwise (reason says why). checks lists what was established, each true or false; not_checked lists what this record does not cover. measurement, when present, is the last recorded image, compose and model digests with their transparency-log and on-chain state; attested_now says whether they are what the provider is attested as running now. Nothing here is the provider's own claim repeated back.

get.summary: An attestation badge image for a provider or a model
get.description: Public, for an tag or a Markdown image. id is a provider id or a model id (author/slug). The status a prompt is served under right now: attested (a fresh attestation the router verified itself and attested retention), policy, vendor-forwarded, or unverified (unknown id, simulated evidence, or nothing current). While attested it also shows the first eight hex characters of the verified measurement (compose hash, else image digest) and of the classifier policy hash the attestation bound, and the share of the last 7 days with a fresh attestation, truncated. Only site colours, no script and no external reference. An unknown id is still an image, reading Unverified, with status 404. Nothing is checked in the viewer's browser; /badge.js does that.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A provider id, or a model id such as meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct.

get.summary: Proof-time: how long each attesting provider has held a fresh attestation
get.description: Public. For every live or shadow provider that has a TEE and an attestation endpoint: the current status (by the same rule as GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}), and the share of the last 24 hours and 7 days in which the router held a fresh attestation it verified itself. A fresh attestation is one the router verified at most fresh_within_ms ago (three attestor intervals) with no failed run since; a failed run, or evidence accepted only as simulated, ends the cover at once. share is the covered part of the time the record spans (observed_ms); when the record does not reach back to the start of the window (history_complete false) the earlier time is unknown and counts neither way, and share is null when nothing is recorded. buckets divides the window into equal slices, each the percent covered, or null before the record begins. Also: measurement changes in the last 7 days, the last measurement change (which fields, from and to), the last failed check as a code with a fixed message (never the provider's own text), the pass rate of the last 7 days' checks, and the latest health-probe and canary outcomes. Nothing here is raw provider output. Returns 501 not_enabled when the router keeps no history (ATTESTATION_HISTORY_DAYS is 0).

501.description: not_enabled: this router keeps no attestation history.

get.summary: A provider's recorded attestation, canary and probe events
get.description: Public. Newest first. Each event is one attestor run (kind attestation: ok or a failure code, the report hash, the TLS pin's SPKI hash when pinned, the verifiers that accepted the quote, the digests the run reported and whether they differ from the previous run's), one canary run (kind canary), or a change of the health probe's outcome (kind probe; only changes are recorded). Events are kept for history_days. Page with before set to the previous page's next: it encodes the moment and id of the last event, so events at the same instant are neither skipped nor repeated. Returns 404 for an unknown provider and 501 not_enabled when the router keeps no history.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The next value of the previous page.

parameters.name: ok
parameters.description: Only events that passed (true) or failed (false).

501.description: not_enabled: this router keeps no attestation history.

get.summary: The key measurement bundles must be signed with
get.description: Public; 404 until the router is configured with a measurement key. A measurement bundle names the compose hash, source commit and tarball hash, model digest and image digests of a provider's attested software, with an MRTD and RTMR3 allow-list. It counts only if it is signed with this ECDSA P-256 key (SHA-256, DER signature over the bundle's canonical JSON) and the entry recording it in the transparency log verifies. key_id is the SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

get.summary: A provider's signed measurement bundles and their transparency-log entries
get.description: Public; 404 until the router is configured with a measurement key. Newest first. Each item carries the bundle, its signature and digest, the status the router reached (pending, verified or rejected, with the reason), the log entry it verified (uuid, index, integration time, whether the inclusion proof, checkpoint signature and signed entry timestamp verified) and, once verified, the log's own copy of the entry (entry_record: body, inclusion proof, signed entry timestamp) so a verifier can check it without asking the log.

post.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request: initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call (list_models, list_attested_models, chat, verify_provider, get_receipt, verify_receipt), plus notifications, which get an empty 202. Replies are JSON, never a stream; there are no sessions. Only the chat tool needs an API key, which it spends like /api/v1/chat/completions. chat takes lane (public or attested) and disclosure (none, policy or any), meaning provider.lane and provider.disclosure: on the attested lane a prompt goes only to a provider with a fresh attestation the router verified and attested retention, and when none can answer the tool returns an error (no_attested_endpoint or disclosure_unavailable; nothing sent, nothing charged). Its result reports lane, the disclosure class the receipt records and, for an attested gateway, upstream_attestation (attested, gpu_attested, receipt_verified). list_attested_models lists the models the attested lane can serve now, with gpu_attested (true, false, or null before any verified gateway receipt). verify_provider takes provider_id and returns the router's attestation record for it in plain terms: status, TEE, verifiers, TLS pin, transparency-log status and not_checked; it is the same record as GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}. A connection can be made attested by default with the lane query parameter or the X-Anyroute-Lane header on the /mcp URL (disclosure and X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max set a ceiling): the strictest setting wins, a call cannot relax it, and an unrecognised value refuses the chat call. Malformed JSON or a batch gets HTTP 400, a request carrying a foreign Origin header gets 403 and GET gets 405; all three carry a JSON-RPC error body.

parameters.name: lane
parameters.description: Connection default for the chat tool: public (default) or attested. attested sends every chat prompt only to attested providers and refuses the call when none can answer. Repeat or combine with the header: the strictest applies. unlinkable is not available over MCP.

parameters.name: disclosure
parameters.description: Connection default disclosure ceiling for the chat tool: none, policy or any (default). The strictest of this, the header and the call's own setting applies.

parameters.name: X-Anyroute-Lane
parameters.description: Same as the lane query parameter.

parameters.name: X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max
parameters.description: Same as the disclosure query parameter.

200.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response: a result, or an error object with a JSON-RPC code.

202.description: Notification accepted; the body is empty.

get.summary: List the account's saved routes

get.summary: A provider's disclosure profile and the class it is served under right now
get.description: Public. Every value is what the operator documented, with its own source and date; nothing is inferred from traffic. A provider with no recorded profile returns the conservative defaults (retention logs, jurisdiction unknown, legal hold undeclared, training use unknown, declared false). current.class is attested only when retention is declared attested and the provider's TEE attestation is fresh now; current.simulated is true when that attestation is a development report (never accepted in production).

put.summary: Replace a provider's disclosure profile (operator only)
put.description: Requires the operator token in X-Admin-Token or as a bearer token; an API key is not accepted. The profile is replaced as a whole: a claim that is left out reverts to its conservative default. A retention other than logs needs a legal_hold claim, and retention attested needs a provider with a TEE and attestation endpoint.

409.description: provider_not_attestable: retention attested was claimed for a provider with no TEE or attestation endpoint (or a development TEE in production).

put.summary: Declare a model's variant, license and weights provenance (operator only)
put.description: Requires the operator token in X-Admin-Token or as a bearer token; an API key is not accepted. The record is replaced as a whole. The model need not be listed by any provider yet: classify it first. native_low_refusal and abliterated are restricted variants and need license and base_model on record. status candidate routes the model to no provider until the record is written again as servable.

get.summary: Day-zero candidates and their latest scores (operator only)
get.description: Requires the operator token. When enabled, the router watches Hugging Face for new fine-tunes of the base models it is configured with, keeps those whose model card carries an allowed license (MIT or Apache-2.0 by default) and records why it rejected the rest. Status: discovered, rejected, evaluated, failed, approved or servable.

get.summary: One day-zero candidate (operator only)

put.summary: Say which provider offer serves a candidate's weights (operator only)
put.description: The offer's model must declare the candidate's Hugging Face repository as its hugging_face_id, so an evaluation of one set of weights cannot approve a different model. From the moment a repository is a candidate, a model that declares it is routed to no provider until the candidate is servable.

409.description: repo_mismatch: the offer's model does not declare the candidate's repository. candidate_rejected: the candidate was rejected. invalid_state: the candidate is already approved.

post.summary: Run the probe sets against a candidate's endpoint (operator only)
post.description: Sends the endpoint 16 benign prompts that base models commonly over-refuse (fiction, security education, medical and legal information; none harmful or illegal), 12 capability prompts with exact checks (arithmetic, JSON format, instruction following) and the router's canary set. The scores are stored. The candidate passes when its refusal rate is at most DAYZERO_MAX_REFUSAL_RATE, its capability score at least DAYZERO_MIN_CAPABILITY, its canary accuracy at least DAYZERO_MIN_CANARY and the canary precision check does not contradict the declared quantization. An approved or servable candidate that fails loses its approval and stops being served.

409.description: no_endpoint: link an endpoint first. endpoint_unavailable: the linked offer or provider is not live. candidate_rejected: the candidate was rejected.
invalid_state: only an evaluated candidate can be approved.

post.summary: Make an approved candidate servable (operator only)
post.description: Succeeds only if the linked provider is served under attested retention with a fresh attestation and its attestation reports the in-enclave classifier as enabled: the same test routing applies to a request. Otherwise 409 not_servable says why and nothing changes. The router repeats this for approved candidates on every day-zero run.

409.description: invalid_state: only an approved candidate can be promoted. not_servable: no attested provider that reports the classifier serves it now; error.metadata.candidate is the candidate.

post.summary: Get a challenge to claim a model's creator royalty
post.description: Public and rate limited. The model must have a Hugging Face weights source on record. Commit file_content to the file named in file, on the main branch of hugging_face_id, then call the verify endpoint before expires_at. The address is the one that will receive the royalty.

hf_handle.description: Optional: refused if it is not the owner of the weights source.

409.description: not_claimable: the model has no Hugging Face weights source on record.

get.summary: Read a creator claim

post.summary: Check the published challenge and record the royalty recipient
post.description: Public and rate limited. The router reads the repository's owner and the claim file through the Hugging Face API. The owner must still be the handle the challenge was issued to and the file must contain the challenge on its own line. On success the address becomes the model's royalty recipient at the router's default rate (5 percent unless configured otherwise, at most 20 percent): it is registered in the royalty contract first when one is configured, then recorded, and every later call to the model includes the royalty in its price. Verifying a verified claim returns it again.

409.description: claim_stale: the model's weights source changed since the challenge was issued.

410.description: claim_expired: the challenge is no longer valid; start a new claim.

502.description: chain_failed: the royalty contract registration failed and nothing was recorded; verify again. hf_unavailable: Hugging Face could not be read.

get.summary: Issuer keys, the token challenge and token prices
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables blind tokens. One 2048-bit RSA issuer key per denomination (1000, 10000 and 100000 token-units) per epoch (a week), published before the epoch starts. token_key_id is the SHA-256 of the key's RFC 9578 SubjectPublicKeyInfo (token_key, base64url), so a client can check the key against its id. A key issues only while its status is issuing; its tokens stay redeemable until redeem_until. Every token must carry challenge_digest, the SHA-256 of the published challenge. commitments are the per-epoch values a BlindIssuer contract records. Nothing in this response is signed: compare commitments with a value recorded independently (for example on chain) before trusting the keys.

post.description: Debits the key's credits through the ledger and returns one blind signature per blinded message, in order. The client blinds the token inputs (RFC 9474) with the key named by token_key_id, and unblinds the signatures locally; the router stores counts only, never the blinded messages, the signatures or the tokens. Sending the same request again after a lost response returns the same signatures without charging again (replayed: true). Purchases count against the key's budget and are rate limited per key, capped per request (max_batch) and per account per day. A key restricted to some models cannot buy tokens. 404 unless the router enables blind tokens.

409.description: The key's epoch is not open yet (epoch_not_open), has ended (epoch_closed) or was revoked (token_key_revoked), or the same purchase is still being processed (purchase_in_progress).

get.summary: Gateway key configuration (RFC 9458 section 3)
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. One key configuration in application/ohttp-keys form: key identifier, KEM (DHKEM X25519 HKDF-SHA256), public key, and the KDF and AEAD pairs offered (HKDF-SHA256 with AES-128-GCM). The key changes every epoch (a day by default) and keeps opening requests for a grace period after that. This response is not signed: check it against the signed key list (GET /api/v1/ohttp/key-list) before use. Also served at /.well-known/ohttp-gateway.

503.description: The gateway has no usable key right now (ohttp_no_key). Retry after Retry-After.

post.summary: Oblivious HTTP gateway: unwrap an encapsulated request, serve it, wrap the response
post.description: Sent by a relay (or, without the privacy benefit, directly). The body is a message/ohttp-req: a binary HTTP request (RFC 9292) sealed to the gateway key. The gateway serves it on the router's own routes and answers 200 with a message/ohttp-res that carries the whole inner response, errors included, so an inner 4xx is inside the encapsulation. Reachable routes: POST chat/completions and completions (streaming only with chunked Oblivious HTTP), POST embeddings, POST blind/purchase, GET blind/keys, GET models; anything else is an inner 404 route_not_allowed. Of the request's headers only Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, X-Anyroute-Lane and X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max are passed on. Responses are zero-padded to a multiple of 256 bytes. A relay identifies itself with Authorization: Bearer <key_id>:<secret>; a request without it is treated as direct and is not served the unlinkable lane. Errors before the request could be unwrapped are plain HTTP: 415, 413, 400, 422 (unknown key identifier or a request that does not decrypt, application/problem+json), 401 (a relay credential that is not recognised) and 429. Where the router enables chunked Oblivious HTTP (draft-ietf-ohai-chunked-ohttp; GET /api/v1/relays then lists gateway.chunked), the body may instead be a message/ohttp-chunked-req, answered with a message/ohttp-chunked-res (with Incremental: ?1) that is encrypted and sent chunk by chunk as the inner response is produced, so stream true works; the last chunk is sealed as the final one, so a response that ends without it was cut off and is incomplete. A chunked response that grows past the size limit ends without its final chunk. Do not retry a failed encapsulated request automatically; a repeated ciphertext is answered with an inner 409 replayed_request.

200.description: The encapsulated response: message/ohttp-res for a message/ohttp-req, message/ohttp-chunked-res for a message/ohttp-chunked-req.

413.description: The encapsulated request is larger than the gateway accepts.

415.description: The content type is not message/ohttp-req (or message/ohttp-chunked-req, where the router enables chunked Oblivious HTTP).

422.description: The key identifier is unknown, expired or revoked, the ciphersuite is not offered, or the request does not decrypt with the key it names. Fetch the key configuration again.

get.summary: Gateway key history, signed and hash-chained
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. Every gateway key with its configuration, acceptance window and status, the next epoch's key listed as upcoming before it is served, and the relay list. The document is signed with the router's receipt signing key (Ed25519 over the canonical JSON of data; keys at GET /api/v1/receipts/keys, also registered on chain), and each key's entry_hash chains to the one before it, so a client can pin log.head and notice a key that was removed or replaced. A key's private half is destroyed when its window ends (private_key_destroyed).

get.summary: Relays clients may use for the unlinkable lane
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. Each relay has its operator, its URL and a key_id (an identifier of the credential the relay presents to the gateway, published so it is on record; the router does not verify it beyond authenticating the relay). independent is false for a relay run by the gateway's own operator: the unlinkable lane is not served through it. Pick a relay whose operator is not the gateway operator.

get.summary: $ANYR balance, tier, perks, tier ladder and free credits for the wallet behind this key
get.description: Only keys from wallet sign-in have a wallet; any other key gets the same shape with wallet null and a hint. Tiers apply only when the router sets both ANYR_TOKEN_ADDRESS and HOLDER_TIERS (enabled). The balance is read live (cached for 5 minutes); when it cannot be read, balance_error is true and no tier applies. discount_bps lowers Anyroute's own fee rates (the per-call margin and the BYOK fee), never below 0; prepaid calls carry no margin, so for them the discount is 0.

patch.summary: Update an alert rule (kind cannot change; webhook_url null removes it)

post.description: The Anthropic Messages API, for the Anthropic SDKs and Claude Code (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set to the router). Also served at /api/v1/messages. The request is converted to a chat completion and sent through /api/v1/chat/completions inside the router, so the key, balance, limits, lane, signed receipt and response headers are those of a chat call. Authenticate with x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer. The model is a catalog id (GET /v1/models) or a name the operator mapped with ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP; an unmapped claude-* name is a 404 that says the router serves open models. Text, image (base64 and URL), tool_use and tool_result blocks, tools and tool_choice, stop_sequences, top_k (dropped for a provider that does not list it) and metadata.user_id (sent to the provider as user) are converted; max_tokens above the model's output limit is lowered to it. Tools hosted by Anthropic, thinking and service_tier are accepted and not acted on (named in X-Anyroute-Ignored); PDF documents, mcp_servers and container are refused with a 400. The reply's id is the receipt id, and its anyroute object carries the lane, disclosure class, provider, cost, upstream_attestation where there is one, and the signed receipt. With stream true the events are message_start, ping, content_block_start, content_block_delta (text_delta, input_json_delta), content_block_stop, message_delta (billed usage and the anyroute object) and message_stop, or an error event in place of the ending; a request the router refuses before any output is an HTTP error instead of a stream. stop_reason is end_turn, max_tokens, tool_use or refusal, and stop_sequence only when the provider names the stop string that ended the answer. Errors have Anthropic's shape with an anyroute object carrying the router's own error type.

parameters.name: X-Anyroute-Lane
parameters.description: public (default) or attested. attested sends the prompt only to a provider with a fresh TEE attestation the router verified and attested retention; when none can serve the model the call is refused with 409 (503 while they are down) and nothing is sent or charged. Same meaning as provider.lane; the stricter of the two applies. An unrecognised value is a 400.

parameters.name: X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max
parameters.description: Strictest ceiling on who may see the prompt: none, policy or any (default). Same meaning as provider.disclosure.

200.description: The message, or Anthropic server-sent events when stream is true.

Request-Id.description: An id for this request (req_...), also in the error body's request_id.

X-Anyroute-Ignored.description: Present when the request asked for something that is accepted and not acted on: thinking, service_tier, or tools hosted by Anthropic (tool:<name>). A comma separated list.

schema.description: Anthropic SSE: each event has an event: line naming its type and a data: JSON object.

post.summary: Count the tokens of a message (estimate)
post.description: The body of POST /v1/messages without max_tokens. Returns the router's own estimate of the prompt: about one token for every three characters of text and JSON, plus 1,600 for each image. It is not a tokenizer's count, it costs nothing, and it needs a key. The model is not looked up. Also served at /api/v1/messages/count_tokens.

Request-Id.description: An id for this request (req_...), also in the error body's request_id.

post.description: The OpenAI Responses API, for the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Codex CLI and other Responses clients (POST /v1/responses is the same route). It is an adapter over POST /api/v1/chat/completions: the request is translated and sent to that route in-process with the same credentials and headers, so keys, wallet and per-call payment, blind tokens, limits, disclosure ceilings, lanes, signed receipts and error responses are the chat route's own, and the answer is returned in the Responses shape. With stream true the body is the Responses event stream, each frame an event: line and a data: line carrying type and sequence_number: response.created, response.in_progress, response.output_item.added, response.content_part.added, response.output_text.delta, response.output_text.done, response.content_part.done, response.function_call_arguments.delta, response.function_call_arguments.done, response.custom_tool_call_input.delta and .done, response.output_item.done and last response.completed (or response.incomplete when the answer was cut off by max_output_tokens). A failure after the stream has started is an error event followed by response.failed; there is no [DONE]. Stateless by design: nothing is stored, so store must be false (the default; true is refused), and previous_response_id, conversation, background, stored prompts and file or item references are refused with a 400 whose error.param names the field. Send the whole conversation in input on every request, including function_call and function_call_output items for tool round trips. GET, DELETE and cancel under /api/v1/responses/{id} answer 404. Function tools and custom (freeform) tools run. A custom tool, such as Codex's apply_patch, is offered to the model as a function with one string argument, input; its description, a line saying it takes freeform text and its grammar, if it has one, become the function's description, as guidance only: no grammar is enforced. A call to it comes back as a custom_tool_call item with the text as input (streamed as response.custom_tool_call_input.delta, then response.custom_tool_call_input.done), and a custom_tool_call_output input item is its result on the next turn. Hosted tools (web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, computer_use, image_generation, mcp) are refused with a 400 naming the tool, because AnyRoute hosts none; run the work in your own code and return it as a function_call_output or custom_tool_call_output. Route with provider (lane, disclosure and the router's other preferences) or the X-Anyroute-Lane header; the stricter of the two applies, and a request no provider can serve under the lane is refused (409 lane_unavailable) with nothing sent and nothing charged. The response carries X-Receipt-Id, Inference-Id and X-Anyroute-Lane (and X-Anyroute-Policy-Hash where the serving endpoint attested one), and its metadata carries anyroute_receipt_id, anyroute_lane and, once known, anyroute_disclosure. Other Responses options (include, truncation, service_tier, prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier, stream_options) are accepted and ignored.

200.description: A Response object, or the Responses event stream when stream is true.

X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Present when an x402 payment was settled for this call: base64 JSON {success, transaction, network, payer}.

schema.description: SSE frames (event: and data: lines) in the order described above; the response.completed, response.incomplete and response.failed frames carry the whole Response object.

get.summary: Not available: responses are not stored
get.description: Always 404 (responses_not_stored), like DELETE and POST .../cancel and GET .../input_items on this path. AnyRoute is stateless: it stores no responses, conversations or input items, so there is nothing to retrieve. A response is returned by the call that creates it. The call's signed receipt, which holds no prompt or answer, is at GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}: the id is in the X-Receipt-Id header and the response's metadata.anyroute_receipt_id.

post.summary: Answer a question from documents you send, keeping nothing
post.description: Retrieval-augmented answers over documents sent with the question, with nothing kept. The router cuts the documents into overlapping chunks, embeds the chunks and the question through POST /api/v1/embeddings (in batches), ranks the chunks by cosine similarity in memory, and answers from the best top_k through POST /api/v1/chat/completions, citing numbered sources. Every call is an ordinary call of your key: billed, limited, routed by lane and receipted, and the response lists every receipt id with its lane, the disclosure class it was served under and, for an attested gateway, its upstream_attestation check. Needs a prepaid API key (Authorization: Bearer); per-call payment and blind tokens are not accepted. Lane: send provider.lane (public or attested) or provider.disclosure (none, policy, any), or the X-Anyroute-Lane and X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max headers, and every call is held to exactly that and refused, never downgraded: on the attested lane 503 no_attested_endpoint (error.metadata.reason none_attested, or attested_endpoints_down with Retry-After); with only a disclosure ceiling 409 disclosure_unavailable, or 503 disclosure_provider_unavailable while qualifying providers are down; or 502 upstream_not_attested when an attested gateway's receipt does not show an attested upstream (the reply is withheld and the call is billed). A lane or ceiling pinned on the key (routing.provider) applies to every step, not only the chat call. A model the router resolves itself (a saved route, an alias of the key, anyroute/...) can pin a lane of its own, so a request naming one must state provider.lane (400 lane_required). Send none and the attested lane is used when the chat model and the embedding model both have an attested endpoint; otherwise the public lane is used and lane_note says why. embedding_model defaults to qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b, else the cheapest embedding model, preferring models with an attested endpoint. Unlinkable is not available. An error from a step is that step's own status and error.type, with error.metadata.step (embeddings or chat) and error.metadata.receipts, the calls already made and billed. Caps (configurable): 200 documents, 2 MiB of document text, 2000 chunks and 64 embeddings calls per request, 413 payload_too_large above them. With stream true the embeddings run first (a refusal there, or at the start of the chat call, is an ordinary JSON error); the stream then sends a chat.completion.chunk event with choices [] and rag.object rag.sources (the sources and the embeddings receipts), the chat stream exactly as /api/v1/chat/completions sends it, an event with rag.object rag.summary (all receipts, totals and, if the chat call was refused mid-stream, error), and data: [DONE]. Nothing of the documents, the question or the answer is stored. The documents, their chunks and vectors and the question live in the memory of the one request that carries them and are dropped when it ends; this endpoint writes them to no database, cache or file, does not log them and never uses the response cache. What remains is what any call leaves: each embeddings call and the chat call is a generation of the key, with a signed receipt holding ids, model, provider, lane, token counts, cost, timing and the SHA-256 of the request and of the response, not their text (a hash confirms an exact guess; it does not reveal text). The text does leave the router: the chunks and the question go to the embedding model's provider and the question and the best chunks go to the chat model's provider. What those providers see and keep depends on the lane; on the attested lane only providers with attested retention and a fresh attestation the router verified are used, which shows what code is running, not what it does with the text.

200.description: The answer, its sources and the receipt of every call; or, with stream true, Server-Sent Events: a chat.completion.chunk with choices [] and rag.object rag.sources, the chat stream, a chunk with rag.object rag.summary, then data: [DONE]. The headers are those of the chat call, except X-Anyroute-Disclosure, which is the weakest class among all the calls (and is left out when a call's class is not known), and X-Anyroute-Policy-Hash, which is sent only when every call reported the same one.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events; each data: line is a JSON object of the chat.completion.chunk shape.

409.description: No provider meets provider.disclosure for a step (disclosure_unavailable), or no embedding model does. Nothing was sent to a provider for that step. error.metadata.step names it and error.metadata.receipts lists the calls already made.

413.description: More documents, bytes of document text, chunks or embeddings calls than the router allows in one request (payload_too_large). error.metadata.limit is the cap. Nothing was sent.

502.description: A step failed after the router accepted the request: upstream_not_attested (an attested gateway's receipt did not show an attested upstream; the reply was withheld and the call is billed), providers_unavailable, or invalid_embedding_response. error.metadata.step and error.metadata.receipts say where it stopped and what was billed.

get.summary: Newest checkpoint, with the cosignatures collected so far
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables the transparency log. A C2SP signed note: the checkpoint text (origin, tree size, base64 root hash; no extension lines), a blank line, the log's Ed25519 signature line, then one cosignature/v1 line per configured witness that has cosigned this tree size. Verify the log's line against the log key pinned out of band (GET /api/v1/tlog shows it, but a client must not take it from the log it is checking), and count witness lines against the witness keys you trust. Served with Cache-Control: no-cache.

text/plain.example:
router.example/tlog
12
q0qBmQ4H0cMA5Tq3kQ0V8wQv1c5V3bI1n4r7FQ0y2Hc=

— router.example/tlog <base64 key id and signature>
— witness.example/w1 <base64 key id, timestamp and cosignature>

get.summary: Merkle tree tile (tlog-tiles, height 8)
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables the transparency log, and for any tile or width the tree does not have yet. The concatenated 32-byte node hashes of tree level 8 x level, indices 256 x N to 256 x N + W. The index path is the tlog-tiles encoding of N (groups of three digits, all but the last prefixed with x: 1234067 is x001/x234/067) and may end in .p/<W> for a partial tile of width 1 to 255. A tile of a given width never changes, so tiles are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The encoded tile index, optionally followed by .p/<width>; it may contain slashes.

get.summary: Entry bundle (tlog-tiles)
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables the transparency log. The entries at leaf indices 256 x N to 256 x N + W, each as a big-endian 16-bit length followed by the entry: the canonical JSON {v, type: "anyroute.tlog.entry", kind, sha256, key}, whose leaf hash is SHA-256(0x00 || entry). Same index encoding and caching as the hash tiles.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The encoded tile index, optionally followed by .p/<width>; it may contain slashes.

get.summary: The log: origin, verifier key, witnesses, quorum and newest checkpoint
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables the transparency log. What entry kinds exist and which witnesses the router collects cosignatures from. Pin the log's verifier key and the witness keys from a source other than the log itself. With Rekor anchoring on (TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED), rekor names the anchoring key and the newest anchored checkpoint's Rekor entry; it is null otherwise.

get.summary: Newest checkpoint cosigned by the witness quorum
get.description: Public; 404 (not_witnessed) until some checkpoint carries cosignatures from at least TLOG_WITNESS_QUORUM configured witnesses. Same note format as /tlog/checkpoint.

text/plain.example:
router.example/tlog
12
q0qBmQ4H0cMA5Tq3kQ0V8wQv1c5V3bI1n4r7FQ0y2Hc=

— router.example/tlog <base64 key id and signature>
— witness.example/w1 <base64 key id, timestamp and cosignature>

get.summary: One checkpoint with its cosignatures
get.description: Public; 404 (unknown_checkpoint) when the log never signed a checkpoint of that tree size.

text/plain.example:
router.example/tlog
12
q0qBmQ4H0cMA5Tq3kQ0V8wQv1c5V3bI1n4r7FQ0y2Hc=

— router.example/tlog <base64 key id and signature>
— witness.example/w1 <base64 key id, timestamp and cosignature>

get.summary: The entry for a key or configuration
get.description: Public; 404 (not_logged) when the key is not in the log. sha256 is the digest a client computes from what it holds: the raw Ed25519 receipt key, the encoded Oblivious HTTP key configuration, the blind issuer SubjectPublicKeyInfo (its token_key_id), the canonical measurement bundle, or the canonical JSON of a sidecar's bindings.

get.summary: An entry with its inclusion proof and, on request, a consistency proof
get.description: Public. The entry for (kind, sha256), a checkpoint that includes it (by default the newest one the witness quorum cosigned, else, with Rekor anchoring on, the newest anchored one, else the newest one), the RFC 6962 inclusion proof to that checkpoint's root and, with from, the consistency proof between tree size from and the checkpoint's size. Nothing here is trusted by itself: a client checks the log signature and witness cosignatures (or, with anchoring, the checkpoint's Rekor entry in checkpoint.rekor) on the checkpoint, recomputes the leaf from the entry and verifies both proofs. 404 not_logged, 409 not_yet_included when the requested checkpoint predates the entry.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Prove against the checkpoint of this tree size instead.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The tree size of the newest checkpoint the client already holds.

409.description: The chosen checkpoint does not include the entry yet (not_yet_included).

get.summary: Consistency proof between two tree sizes
get.description: Public. The RFC 6962 consistency proof from tree size from to tree size to (to at most the current size). Witnesses use it before cosigning; clients use it to check that a newer checkpoint extends one they saw.

post.summary: A witness hands in its cosignature on a checkpoint
post.description: Public, rate limited per client address (TLOG_COSIGN_RPM). The body is the checkpoint note as the log served it with the witness's cosignature/v1 line added (the C2SP tlog-cosignature format: key id, 8-byte timestamp and Ed25519 signature over "cosignature/v1\ntime <t>\n" and the checkpoint text). Only lines from witnesses in TLOG_WITNESSES count; each valid one is kept, the newest per witness and tree size. A witness should cosign only after verifying a consistency proof from the last checkpoint it cosigned (scripts/tlog-witness.ts does). 400 invalid_checkpoint or unknown_log, 403 unknown_witness or invalid_cosignature, 404 unknown_checkpoint, 409 checkpoint_mismatch when the text is not what the log signed for that size.

409.description: The note is not the checkpoint the log signed for that size (checkpoint_mismatch).

413.description: The note is larger than 16 KiB (payload_too_large).

get.summary: Rekor anchoring: the anchoring key, the newest anchored checkpoint and a list of anchors
get.description: Public; 404 (rekor_not_enabled) unless the router anchors its checkpoints in Rekor (TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED). Each checkpoint the log moves to is recorded, at most once per TLOG_REKOR_MIN_INTERVAL_MS, as a hashedrekord entry in the Sigstore Rekor log at rekor_url: the entry holds the SHA-256 of the checkpoint as the log signed it (the checkpoint text, a blank line and the log's own signature line, without cosignatures) and an ECDSA P-256 signature over it by the anchoring key. The router verifies the entry's inclusion proof (and, with REKOR_PUBLIC_KEY, Rekor's signed checkpoint and signed entry timestamp) before it lists it. anchors lists every verified anchor, newest checkpoint first; page with before=next_before. Anyone can compare the entries the anchoring key has in Rekor with this list: an entry the list does not explain, or two anchored checkpoints of one size with different roots, is a split view.

parameters.description: Only anchors of checkpoints smaller than this tree size.

get.summary: The anchoring key (ECDSA P-256)
get.description: Public; 404 (rekor_not_enabled) unless the router anchors its checkpoints in Rekor (TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED). The public key that signs the log's Rekor entries, and its key_id (SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo, hex). Every entry carries this key, so it can be searched for in Rekor. A client that checks anchors pins this key out of band. Served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=300.

post.summary: Create a batch of chat or embeddings requests, run in the background at a discount
post.description: Also at POST /v1/batches. The OpenAI Batch API shape without files: send the lines inline as requests (a list) or input_jsonl (JSON Lines text), one request per line with a unique custom_id (at most 64 characters), method POST, a url of /v1/chat/completions or /v1/embeddings (the /api/v1 forms are accepted too) and the request body. endpoint, when given, must match every line's url. input_file_id is refused with 400: there is no files endpoint, so send requests or input_jsonl. stream true, council mode (model anyroute/council) and verify are refused in a batch. A batch with an invalid line is not created: the 400 invalid_request carries error.metadata.errors, a list of { line, code, message } with 1-based line numbers. Needs a prepaid key. The lines run on the router's worker in spare capacity, so a batch can take minutes; lines not run within the 24h completion window expire and are not charged. Each line is billed at 50% of the normal price (BATCH_DISCOUNT_BPS 5000), a failed line is not charged, and every answered line gets its own signed receipt. Lanes, provider preferences, key budgets and key rate limits apply to each line exactly as to a normal call. Limits (operator settings): BATCH_MAX_LINES (1000 lines), BATCH_MAX_BYTES (8 MiB of input) and BATCH_MAX_ACTIVE (2 unfinished batches per key; one more is refused with 429 batch_limit); a batch over the line or byte limit is refused. The request lines and answers are never written to the database: until the results expire they are kept sealed (AES-256-GCM, with a key derived from the router's secret) in Redis, or in the router's memory without Redis, and then deleted. The database keeps only counts, costs, statuses and generation ids.
