BadRequest.description: The request body, JSON or parameters failed validation. error.type is, for example, invalid_request, invalid_json or invalid_guardrails; do not retry the same request unchanged.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication is missing or was rejected: no API key, an unknown, disabled or expired key, or invalid wallet authentication. error.type is missing_key, invalid_key, key_disabled, key_expired or invalid_wallet_auth.

PaymentRequired.description: The call cannot be paid: the balance or the key's budget is insufficient (insufficient_credits, key_budget_exceeded), or a per-call payment is required or was not accepted (payment_required, payment_pending, payment_insufficient, payment_unknown_quote, payment_failed). A payment_required quote is in error.metadata and binds to this exact request; never repeat a payment automatically.

X-Payment-Required.description: Present on a per-call payment quote; names the payment asset.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Present on a per-call payment quote; carries the chain and quote nonce.

Forbidden.description: The key is valid but may not do this: its role does not allow the action, or its model allowlist excludes the model. error.type is forbidden or model_not_allowed.

NotFound.description: The model, provider route, key, team, generation or receipt does not exist or is not visible to the caller. error.type is, for example, not_found, model_not_found or no_providers.

DisclosureUnavailable.description: 409 disclosure_unavailable. No provider meets provider.disclosure, though the model has providers that would otherwise serve the request (a lane that no attested endpoint can serve is 503 no_attested_endpoint instead). On chat completions it can also be verification_unavailable: verify "dual" found fewer than two providers of the model that support temperature and seed (on lane attested: fewer than two different attested providers of the model). The request is never routed to a provider that does not meet the setting; nothing was sent to any provider and nothing was charged.

LaneNotAvailable.description: 501 lane_not_available. Lane unlinkable is not available on this router: it needs the Oblivious HTTP gateway, or the lane over its Tor onion service, with blind tokens, which it does not run. Nothing was sent to any provider.

DisclosureProviderDown.description: 503. no_attested_endpoint: lane attested or unlinkable, and no endpoint of the model with a fresh, verified attestation can serve it; error.metadata.reason is none_attested, or attested_endpoints_down (with Retry-After) when attested endpoints exist but are all in an outage. A council with an attested seat (a member or the judge) that has none is refused the same way, and error.metadata.council_seat names the seat. disclosure_provider_unavailable: providers that meet provider.disclosure exist but are all in an outage right now; retry after Retry-After. Either way the request is not routed to any other provider and nothing was charged.

TooManyRequests.description: A rate limit was reached (rate_limited). Wait for the Retry-After interval before retrying.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, when the limit reports it.

AnthropicError.description: Anthropic's error shape, for the Messages endpoints. error.type follows the status: 400 invalid_request_error, 401 authentication_error, 402 billing_error, 403 permission_error, 404 not_found_error, 413 request_too_large, 429 rate_limit_error (with Retry-After), 5xx api_error, 504 timeout_error. A status Anthropic does not define keeps its own (409 for a lane no provider can serve, 501 for a lane the router does not run) and sends X-Should-Retry: false. anyroute carries the router's own error type and metadata, and the receipt_id when a refused call was billed.

Request-Id.description: An id for this request (req_...), also in the error body's request_id.

OllamaError.description: Ollama's error shape, {"error": "..."}, with the router's status: 400 for a bad field (the message names it), 401 or 402 without a usable key, 404 for an unknown model (the message names one to use), 409 or 503 when the requested lane cannot be served, 429 with Retry-After, 501 for local-model operations, 502 when every provider failed before any output.

admission.description: Null for curated providers. Approval requires admitted probation/live status, no refusal reasons and a fresh successful latest hardware attestation plus the recorded checked policy.

policy_version.description: Version recorded by admission or renewal, not necessarily the latest published policy.

admission.description: Null for curated providers. Approval requires admitted probation/live status, no refusal reasons and a fresh successful latest hardware attestation plus the recorded checked policy.

policy_version.description: Version recorded by admission or renewal, not necessarily the latest published policy.

attestation_history.description: First 50 sanitized events from the existing attestation history endpoint, with data, next cursor, history_days and url. Null when history is disabled.

measurement.description: Existing attestation endpoint current measurement: digests, status, timestamps, hardware registers, registry state and transparency_log with Rekor entry_url and verification checks; no raw quote.

items.description: Existing attestation endpoint superseded measurements, each with its own superseded_at and transparency_log entry_url.

proof_time.description: Existing proof-time summary metadata (generated_at, history_days, fresh_within_ms) and its host record. Host is null when absent from that summary. Proof-time itself is null when history is disabled.

operator.description: Present only after walletAuth recovers the stored provider operator. Lifetime invoice units include paid invoices; unpaid units have no recorded payment transaction and can include a pending payout.

pricing.description: Prices are returned as decimal strings per token; consult the live response.

lanes.description: The lanes this model can be served on right now: public whenever it has a live endpoint; attested while one of its endpoints has attested retention and a fresh, verified attestation; unlinkable as well where the router serves that lane (Oblivious HTTP, or its Tor onion service). The endpoints listing carries the same field per endpoint.

disclosure.description: How many live endpoints are served under each disclosure class right now.

creator.description: Address that receives the model's creator royalty, once claimed.

royalty_bps.description: Creator royalty in basis points of the notional price; 0 until a creator is recorded.

variant.description: native_low_refusal and abliterated are restricted: they are routed only to providers served under attested retention with a fresh attestation whose attestation reported the in-enclave hard-block classifier as enabled. Whatever lane or disclosure setting a request carries, and however the provider is pinned, they are never sent to a public or vendor-forwarded provider.

variant_source.description: declared: an operator recorded the variant. candidate: the model is the weights of a day-zero candidate. inferred: nobody has classified the model and its name says its refusals were removed, so it is treated as abliterated. default: no record, treated as mainstream.

license.description: License identifier from the weights' model card, when an operator recorded one.

base_model.description: The model these weights derive from.

weights.description: Where the weights came from, as recorded by the operator.

revision.description: Commit the weights were taken from.

digest.description: sha256:<hex> of the weights, when recorded (for a day-zero model, the model digest in the provider's verified attestation).

creator_handle.description: Hugging Face handle of the uploader.

datacenter_region.description: The one datacenter region every live endpoint of the model reports; null when any endpoint does not report one or they differ.

routing_variants.description: Model suffixes that change how this model is routed right now: nitro (fastest providers first, as provider.sort throughput) and floor (cheapest first, as provider.sort price) always; free while a free endpoint serves it; private while an endpoint has a fresh TEE attestation.

ModelAttestation.description: What the strongest live endpoint serving the model has proven. Every value comes from the router's own attestation and measurement records; a value that is not known is null, never filled in. null when no endpoint serves the model.

best.description: The strongest disclosure class any live endpoint is served under right now (the same value as disclosure.best).

manifest_ref.description: Where that endpoint's measured image is recorded, while its attestation is fresh. null when neither is known.

rekor_entry.description: The transparency log entry uuid, once its inclusion proof was checked.

registry_tx.description: The on-chain MeasurementRegistry transaction, once the registry reports the measurement.

exec_profile_id.description: The attested execution profile. null until an attestation the router checks reports one.

policy_hash.description: The classifier policy hash that endpoint's fresh attestation bound (as sent in X-Anyroute-Policy-Hash), else null.

model.description: Public model ID, optionally with routing suffixes: :nitro sorts providers by throughput (fastest first) and :floor by price (cheapest first), the same as provider.sort throughput and price and winning over it; both only order the providers the other preferences and the lane allow. :free and :private also apply. The reserved ID anyroute/council selects council mode when the router enables it. @route/<slug> calls a saved route and @preset/<name> (or @preset/<name>@<version> to pin one version) calls a preset of the key's account. @character/<id> calls a character: the card is the prompt and models[0], or the character's default model, answers.

tools.description: Requires a model/provider that supports tools.

response_format.description: Requires a model/provider that supports the requested response format.

verify.description: Send the same request to two providers of the model at temperature 0 with a fixed seed and compare the outputs. Both calls are billed. Needs the router's council feature; not combinable with stream, models, cache or n above 1. Provider preferences, disclosure ceiling and lane apply to both calls. With lane attested the two calls go to two different attested providers of the model (retention declared attested, attestation fresh); each receipt then records its provider's attestation as payload.attestation_ref, and the verification field carries attested and attestation_refs next to agree. If two such providers do not exist the answer is 409, and nothing is sent or charged.

CouncilRequest.description: Used with model anyroute/council. Members are called in parallel through the normal routing path, then the judge chooses one answer (judge) or writes a final one (fuse). Every call is billed and receipted; the worst case of all calls is held up front. provider preferences, including a disclosure ceiling or lane, apply to every member and to the judge.

models.description: Member model IDs. Falls back to the router's configured default when omitted.

judge.description: Model ID of the judge. Falls back to the router's configured default when omitted.

mode.description: judge returns one member's answer unchanged; fuse returns the judge's own text and does not support tools or response_format.

max_cost_usd.description: Refuse the request with 402 council_budget_exceeded unless the worst case of every call fits. Lower max_tokens to fit.

min_members.description: Members that must answer before the judge runs. Defaults to 2.

attested.description: true holds every member and the judge to the attested lane (retention declared attested and a fresh attestation the router verified), the same as provider.lane attested for the whole council. Nothing is downgraded or dropped: a member, or the judge, with no attested provider refuses the request with 503 no_attested_endpoint, and nothing is sent or charged. The response then carries attested and attestation_refs in council, and each call's receipt carries attestation_ref. A production router has few attested providers today, so this often returns that 503.

CouncilResult.description: Present on council responses. The top-level receipt is the judge's call and its signed payload carries the same members list; its disclosure is the weakest class among all the calls.

disclosure.description: The class this member was served under.

receipt_id.description: Null for a member that failed; it was not billed.

total_cost.description: USD charged across every member and the judge.

attested.description: Present when the council ran on the attested lane (council.attested true, or lane attested). True only when every member and the judge were served under the attested class and each has a reference in attestation_refs. Signed in the top-level receipt.

attestation_simulated.description: True when any attestation behind the council is a development report; a production router never accepts one.

attestation_refs.description: One entry per call that took part, members in order and then the judge: what the router itself verified about the provider that served it. Signed in the top-level receipt.

label.description: The member's label; absent for the judge.

AttestationRef.description: The attestation the router had verified for a provider when it served a call: the hash of the attestation report and, when the provider attested through a self-signed TLS certificate, the pinned key the router's connection to it accepts. Recorded in the signed receipt of a call made under an attested council or attested dual verification, as payload.attestation_ref. Receipts made any other way do not carry it. The same data is at GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}.

tee.description: tdx, snp, nvidia-cc, tinfoil or dev.

report_hash.description: Hash of the attestation report the router verified (the payload.attestation field of the same receipt).

tls_pin.description: Null when the provider did not attest through a self-signed certificate.

spki_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the pinned certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

attestation_ref.description: SHA-256 of the quote the certificate names.

simulated.description: true when the report is development evidence.

VerificationResult.description: Present on verify "dual" responses. agree is true when both providers returned the same output (exactly, or after whitespace is collapsed); it says nothing about whether either provider is attested, unless the request used lane attested (then attested and attestation_refs say so). The response body is the first provider's output.

attested.description: Present only on lane attested. True when both calls were served by two different providers under the attested class and each has a reference in attestation_refs. Signed in both receipts, next to agree.

attestation_refs.description: One entry per call that ran (label A or B), in the same order as receipts. Each receipt also carries its own provider's reference as payload.attestation_ref.

ProviderPreferences.description: Provider routing preferences (order, only, ignore, sort, max_price, private and others) plus the disclosure options below.

disclosure.description: Ceiling on how a prompt may be handled. none: only providers whose retention is declared attested and whose TEE attestation is fresh. policy: those, plus providers with a documented no-retention policy and no legal hold. any: no filter. Never silently relaxed: if nothing qualifies the request fails (409, or 503 when qualifying providers are down). A request with a ceiling never uses the response cache.

lane.description: public: any endpoint; attested endpoints get attested_bonus (default 1.25) in the selection weight. attested: only endpoints with attested retention and a fresh, verified attestation, with no fallback to any other (503 no_attested_endpoint). unlinkable: the same endpoints, and only for a request that arrived through the Oblivious HTTP gateway by way of an independent relay (see Oblivious HTTP), or through the router's Tor onion service where it serves the lane that way, and is paid with a blind token; 501 where the router serves the lane on neither path, 403 lane_requires_anonymous_auth for an API key or a wallet, 403 unlinkable_requires_relay or unlinkable_requires_independent_relay, 401 unlinkable_requires_token otherwise. Unset: the key's default (routing.provider.lane), then the saved route's, then public; a request through an independent relay paid with a blind token defaults to unlinkable. provider.order, only and ignore still apply inside a lane. On attested and unlinkable the router still terminates TLS and sees the prompt; end-to-end encryption through the router is planned.

lane_downgrade.description: attested: a request for lane unlinkable that carries an API key or a wallet is served on lane attested instead of being refused with lane_requires_anonymous_auth. Never downgrades to public. Same as the X-Anyroute-Lane-Downgrade header; none in either refuses the downgrade.

source.description: The document or statement the value comes from.

as_of.description: The date the source was checked.

declared.description: False when the operator has recorded nothing; every value is then the conservative default.

retention.description: attested: the provider states prompts are not retained and runs in a TEE. policy: a documented no-retention policy. logs: prompts may be logged (default).

jurisdiction.description: Where the operator is subject to legal process; unknown by default.

active.description: null = not declared. A no-retention policy is not trusted while a hold is active or undeclared.

claims.description: The source and date behind each value; null when the value is a default.

simulated.description: True when the attestation behind an attested class is a development report.

DisclosureInput.description: Every claim is optional and carries its own source and date.

management.description: Only honored for authorized authenticated sub-key creation; root-key management is never granted by this field.

tracing.description: Trace export for this key's public-lane calls; null removes it.

role.description: The new key's role in its team (default member). A key cannot hand out a role above its own. In a team with an org budget every key needs a limit that fits.

kid.description: First 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the raw key.

fresh_within_ms.description: How old a verified attestation may be and still count as fresh.

attested.description: Runs that passed with hardware evidence (simulated evidence is not counted).

share.description: Covered part of the time the record spans within the window; null when nothing is recorded.

observed_ms.description: How much of the window the record spans.

history_complete.description: False when the record does not reach back to the start of the window; the earlier time is unknown, not covered and not uncovered.

buckets.description: Equal slices from the start of the window to now (48 for 24h, 84 for 7d): percent covered, or null before the record begins.

share.description: Covered part of the time the record spans within the window; null when nothing is recorded.

observed_ms.description: How much of the window the record spans.

history_complete.description: False when the record does not reach back to the start of the window; the earlier time is unknown, not covered and not uncovered.

buckets.description: Equal slices from the start of the window to now (48 for 24h, 84 for 7d): percent covered, or null before the record begins.

digests.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

from.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

to.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

probe.description: The latest health-probe outcome and when it began.

reason.description: A code from a fixed list with its message; never the provider's own text.

simulated.description: Development evidence: never counted as a fresh attestation.

tls_spki_sha256.description: SPKI hash of the certificate the connection was pinned to, when it was.

measurements.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

measurement_changed.description: The run's digests differ from the previous accepted run's, comparing the fields both report.

next.description: Pass as before for the next page; null on the last page.

verifiers.description: The verifiers that accepted the quote; empty unless status is attested.

policy_hash.description: The classifier policy hash this fresh attestation bound (the value sent as X-Anyroute-Policy-Hash); null unless status is attested and one was bound.

measurement.description: Last recorded digests (image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest), status, attested_now, registers { mrtd, rtmr3 } of the recorded quote, transparency_log { found, inclusion_verified, checkpoint_signature_verified, subject (measurement_bundle or image_digest), entry_url, bundle, ... } and registry { address, state, tx_hash, registered_at }.

payload.description: Signed fields. Among them, disclosure (attested, policy or vendor-forwarded) and lane (public, attested or unlinkable) record how the call was served; attestation_simulated is true when the attestation behind an attested call is a development report. attestation_ref (see AttestationRef) is present on calls made under an attested council or attested dual verification. For a call paid with a blind token, payer is null and nullifier (the SHA-256 of the spent token) and token_key_id are present; nothing names an account. Receipts issued before these fields existed do not carry them.

privacy.description: The privacy label derived from payload for readers. It is not part of what is signed.

ReceiptV2.description: Receipt v2 (spec 0004 Section 4): a COSE_Sign1 over deterministic CBOR claims, signed EdDSA with the same key as v1 (kid is the key id's 8 bytes). claims is the JSON view of exactly what cose signs. Token counts are bucketed; nothing names a payer, an address or content.

chain.description: Streams only: the chunk hash chain head.

policy.description: Present only when the serving endpoint's fresh attestation bound a classifier policy.

cost_units.description: Amount charged in millionths of a US dollar, rounded up.

rid.description: The receipt id the sidecar gave it.

anchored.description: True only when the root was posted on chain and confirmed.

status.description: confirmed: on chain; pending: to be posted (the chain was unreachable); local: kept off chain because no chain is configured.

provider_id_hash.description: keccak256 of the provider id's bytes: the providerId the root is posted under.

attestation_ref.description: 64 hex: SHA-256 of the boot quote the router verified, which every leaf in the root names.

receipt_key.description: The receipt key the quote binds; every leaf in the root verified under it.

window.description: When the router collected the root's leaves: [from, to).

models.description: Catalog model ids in fallback order; no nested @route/.

provider.description: Provider preferences: order, only, ignore, allow_fallbacks, sort (price|latency|throughput), data_collection, zdr, require_parameters, max_price, and the privacy settings lane (public|attested) and disclosure (none|policy|any). For lane and disclosure the stricter of the route and the request applies, so a request can tighten a route but never loosen it; a route on the attested lane is served only by attested providers or refused. lane attested already implies disclosure none.

params.description: Default request parameters from a closed whitelist (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, top_a, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, repetition_penalty, max_tokens, seed, stop, reasoning, verbosity). Prompt fields are rejected.

model.description: Use as the request model, e.g. @route/my-coder.

allowed_models.description: Catalog ids or @route/<slug>; must be within the creator's allowlist.

metadata.description: Labels only, at most 2 KB; prompt-like keys are refused.

SpendReport.description: Spend for the caller's scope (a management key sees its account; other keys see themselves). UTC calendar.

min.description: Minimum balance in whole tokens (decimal string).

rpm_multiplier.description: Multiplies the key's rpm and tpm limits.

discount_bps.description: Lowers Anyroute's own fee rates by this many basis points, never below 0.

challenge_digest.description: SHA-256 of the challenge, hex; the challenge_digest field of every token.

unit_price_usd.description: USD per token-unit for keys created from now on; each key states its own value_usd.

commitment.description: keccak256(abi.encode(uint64 epoch, uint32[] denominations, bytes32[] keyIds)), as recorded by BlindIssuer.commitEpoch.

value_usd.description: What one token of this key is worth; fixed for the key's life.

issued.description: Tokens signed with this key (a count).

keys.description: Oldest first; at most the latest 512.

key_id.description: The 8-bit key identifier: the epoch modulo 256.

entry_hash.description: SHA-256 chain: this entry committed to the one before it.

first_prev.description: The entry hash before the first key listed (64 zeros when the list starts at the first key ever).

key_id.description: A receipt signing key; see GET /api/v1/receipts/keys.

sig.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of data.

key_id.description: Identifier of the credential this relay presents to the gateway.

independent.description: False when the relay's operator is the gateway's own operator.

chunked.description: Present only where the gateway accepts chunked Oblivious HTTP.

token_key_id.description: A key whose status is issuing.

items.description: 256 bytes, base64url: the blinded token input, below the key's modulus.

blinded_msgs.description: Distinct blinded messages, at most max_batch.

replayed.description: True when this exact purchase had already been made; nothing was charged again.

signatures.description: signatures[i] answers blinded_msgs[i]; 256 bytes each, base64url.

enabled.description: Whether holder tiers apply to requests on this router.

wallet.description: The wallet behind this key (wallet sign-in keys only).

balance.description: Token balance in whole tokens (decimal string).

balance_error.description: True when the balance could not be read; no tier applies until it can.

rpm.description: This key's request limit per minute with the multiplier (0 = unlimited).

credits_received.description: Free inference credits paid to this wallet, newest first. They pay for inference only and are not withdrawable.

ModelLaneInput.description: A model's lane record. native_low_refusal and abliterated need license and base_model.

status.description: candidate routes the model to no provider.

source.description: For example huggingface:owner/repo. A creator claim is checked against this repository.

creator_handle.description: Hugging Face handle of the uploader.

revision.description: The revision seen at discovery; the one evaluated.

reason.description: Why a candidate was rejected or failed.

model.description: The catalog model that serves it, once linked.

refusal_rate.description: Share of the benign probe prompts the endpoint refused.

capability_score.description: Share of the exact-check prompts answered correctly.

handle.description: Owner of the repository, from its id.

file.description: File name to commit to the main branch of the repository.

file_content.description: What the file must contain: the challenge on its own line.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS, public address only; stored encrypted.

items.description: A content block: text, image (source base64 or url), tool_use, tool_result, document (text source only); thinking blocks are dropped.

tools.description: Custom tools (name, description, input_schema). Tools hosted by Anthropic are left out and named in X-Anyroute-Ignored.

max_tokens.description: Lowered to the model's output limit, and to what is left of its context, when higher.

top_k.description: Dropped for a provider that does not list it.

user_id.description: Sent to the provider as user.

provider.description: Routing preferences as on chat completions; provider.lane (public or attested) and provider.disclosure work as documented there.

tools.description: Custom tools (name, description, input_schema). Tools hosted by Anthropic are left out and named in X-Anyroute-Ignored.

id.description: The id of the generation's signed receipt (GET /api/v1/receipts/{id}).

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens not read from or written to the provider's cache.

anyroute.description: What the router says about the call.
The router's own error type (for example lane_unavailable), its metadata, and receipt_id when a refused call was billed.

ResponsesInputItem.description: An input item: a message, a function_call or custom_tool_call from an earlier turn, or the function_call_output or custom_tool_call_output for it.

role.description: developer is sent to the model as system.

items.description: input_text ({type, text}), input_image ({type, image_url: an https or data: URL, detail}); output_text and refusal in an earlier assistant message. File ids and input_file are refused.

output.description: The function's result: text, or input_text parts.

input.description: The freeform text the model gave the tool.

ResponsesRequest.description: A Responses API request. Options AnyRoute cannot honour because they need stored state are refused (store true, previous_response_id, conversation, background, prompt) and so is every tool that is not a function or custom tool.

model.description: Public model ID, as in chat completions.

input.description: The whole conversation: one user message as text, or input items. reasoning items are ignored; item_reference and hosted tool items are refused.

instructions.description: Sent as a system message before the input.

format.description: {type: text}, or {type: grammar, syntax: lark or regex, definition}. The grammar is given to the model in the tool's description as guidance and is not enforced.

format.description: text (default), json_object, or json_schema ({type, name, schema, strict, description}), sent as response_format. Requires a model and provider that support it.

reasoning.description: reasoning.effort is passed on as reasoning.effort; providers that do not support it drop it.

metadata.description: Echoed in the Response. Not sent to a provider.

user.description: Passed to the provider as the end-user identity, as in chat completions.

store.description: Must be false or omitted: AnyRoute stores no responses.

ResponsesObject.description: A Response. The request's instructions, tools, tool_choice, max_output_tokens, temperature, top_p, parallel_tool_calls, text, reasoning and user are echoed back; store is always false and previous_response_id null.

status.description: incomplete: the answer was cut off (incomplete_details.reason max_output_tokens or content_filter). failed appears only in a stream, in response.failed.

model.description: The model the router resolved the request to.

input.description: The freeform text the model gave the custom tool.

output.description: A message with output_text, and a function_call or custom_tool_call item for each tool call the model made.

cost.description: What the call cost in USD, as usage.cost in chat completions.

metadata.description: The request's metadata plus anyroute_receipt_id (the id of the signed receipt), anyroute_lane (public, attested or unlinkable), anyroute_disclosure (the class the receipt records, once known) and anyroute_policy_hash (only when the serving endpoint attested one).

RagRequest.description: Unknown fields are refused (400), so a misspelt option is never silently ignored. There is no cache option: the response cache is never used.

documents.description: The text to search: plain strings or {id, text}. At most 200 documents and 2 MiB of UTF-8 text by default (RAG_MAX_DOCUMENTS, RAG_MAX_BYTES). A string, or an object without id, is named doc-<position>, starting at 1. Ids must be unique; a document with no text is refused.

model.description: The chat model that writes the answer. An embedding model is refused.

embedding_model.description: The model that embeds the chunks and the question. Default: qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b if the catalog serves it, else the cheapest embedding model; models with an attested endpoint are considered first unless the request asks for a lane or ceiling, when only models that meet it are.

top_k.description: How many of the best chunks go into the prompt. A request whose largest possible prompt would not fit the chat model's context is refused (400 context_too_small) before anything is embedded.

chunk.description: Sizes are in characters (UTF-16 code units). A chunk ends at a paragraph, line or sentence boundary when there is one in its last 40%, otherwise at a space.

overlap.description: Characters shared by neighbouring chunks: at most half of size. Default: 15% of size.

include_excerpts.description: Return each source's text as excerpt. Off by default: the response then carries where each source lies (start, end) and never the text.

provider.description: The lane and disclosure ceiling, applied to every call. Other routing options are not accepted. If you send none, the lane pinned on the key (routing.provider) is used, and if there is none the router chooses (see the operation description).

lane.description: attested: every call goes only to a provider with attested retention and a fresh attestation the router verified; when one cannot be served the request is refused, never downgraded. unlinkable is not available here (400).

disclosure.description: Same as provider.disclosure on chat completions.

ref.description: The number of the source in the prompt, and in the citations ([1], [2]) the model was asked to make. Sources are in rank order.

chunk_index.description: Position of the chunk within its document, from 0.

score.description: Cosine similarity of the chunk's vector with the question's, rounded to 6 places.

end.description: The chunk is the document text from start to end (characters).

excerpt.description: The chunk's text. Present only when include_excerpts is true.

RagCall.description: One provider call, as its signed receipt records it. Read the receipt with GET /api/v1/receipts/{receipt_id}.

lane.description: The lane the call was made under.

disclosure.description: The class the call was served under, from its receipt.

inputs.description: Embeddings calls: how many texts (the question and chunks) the call embedded.

policy_hash.description: The classifier policy hash the serving endpoint attested, when it did (X-Anyroute-Policy-Hash of that call).

upstream_attestation.description: For an attested gateway: what the router checked of the gateway's receipt for this call. attested is true only when the receipt shows an upstream the gateway verified inside a TEE.

withheld.description: The provider had answered, but the router withheld the reply because the receipt did not show an attested upstream. The call is billed; its signed receipt says why.

attestation_simulated.description: The attestation behind this call is a development report; a production router refuses those.

id.description: The chat call's receipt id: the same as X-Receipt-Id.

receipts.description: Every provider call the request made, in order: the embeddings calls, then the chat call.

lane.description: The lane every call was made under.

lane_source.description: request: you stated a lane or a disclosure ceiling (even public or any) and it was used as stated. default: you stated none, and the router chose attested when the chat model and the embedding model both have an attested endpoint, else public.

lane_note.description: Present when the default lane was public: which model had no known attested endpoint.

disclosure.description: The weakest class among all the calls, from their receipts; null when a call's class is not known.

attestation_simulated.description: Present when any call's attestation was a development report.

note.description: The signed note, as served at /tlog/checkpoint.

cosigned_by.description: Names of the configured witnesses whose cosignatures are attached.

witnessed.description: True when at least the quorum of configured witnesses cosigned.

rekor.description: Present only with Rekor anchoring on: this checkpoint's Rekor entry, or null until it is anchored.

origin.description: Checkpoint origin and the log's key name.

verifier_key.description: Signed-note verifier key <origin>+<key id>+<base64(0x01 || Ed25519 key)>.
<name>+<key id>+<base64(0x04 || Ed25519 key)>, a cosignature/v1 key.

witnessed_size.description: Tree size of the newest checkpoint the quorum cosigned.

rekor.description: Rekor anchoring (TLOG_REKOR_ENABLED): the same fields as GET /api/v1/tlog/rekor without the list; null when anchoring is off.

key_id.description: SHA-256 of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, hex.

public_key_pem.description: The anchoring key, an ECDSA P-256 public key (PEM).

subject.description: The key id, epoch or provider the entry is about.

entry.description: The entry's canonical JSON; its leaf hash is SHA-256(0x00 || these bytes).

subject.description: The key id, epoch or provider the entry is about.

entry.description: The entry's canonical JSON; its leaf hash is SHA-256(0x00 || these bytes).

inclusion.description: RFC 6962 inclusion proof from the entry's leaf to checkpoint.root_hash.

accepted.description: Witnesses whose cosignature on this note verified.

cosignatures.description: Configured witnesses that have now cosigned this tree size.

key_id.description: SHA-256 of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, hex.

public_key_pem.description: The anchoring key, an ECDSA P-256 public key (PEM).

TlogRekorAnchor.description: A Rekor entry that anchors one checkpoint. Rekor's own hashes (inclusion_proof) are hex, as Rekor writes them.

root_hash.description: The checkpoint's root hash, base64 as in checkpoints.

note.description: The artifact: the checkpoint text, a blank line and the log's own signature line.

artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of note; the hash the hashedrekord entry holds (search.sigstore.dev finds the entry by it).

key_id.description: The anchoring key that signed the entry.

uuid.description: The entry's uuid (tree id and leaf hash, hex).

integrated_time.description: When Rekor integrated the entry (seconds since the Unix epoch).

search_url.description: The entry on search.sigstore.dev, for the public Rekor instance.

body.description: The entry body as Rekor returned it; its leaf hash is SHA-256(0x00 || body).

checkpoint.description: Rekor's signed checkpoint for tree_size and root_hash.

verified.description: What the router checked when it stored the entry; checkpoint_signature and signed_entry_timestamp need REKOR_PUBLIC_KEY.

key_id.description: SHA-256 of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, hex.

public_key_pem.description: The anchoring key, an ECDSA P-256 public key (PEM).

min_interval_ms.description: At most one submission to Rekor per this many milliseconds.

latest.description: The newest anchored checkpoint under the current key.

next_before.description: Pass as before for the next page; null on the last page.

PrivacyLabel.description: The privacy label for one answer, computed from its signed receipt (privacyLabel in @anyroute/client computes the same object from a receipt you hold; teeKind and the unlinkable transports are the two things it takes from the router).

lane.description: The lane the receipt records, or null for a receipt that predates lanes.

output.description: Usage unit and quantity from the receipt. Missing unit types default to token; unfamiliar types carry no inferred content-retention guarantee.

participants.description: Provider ids named in an aggregate council receipt; individual receipts describe their access.

router.description: Always true: the router reads the prompt in memory to route it, on every lane.

access.description: attested_enclave: the router had verified the provider's hardware attestation (and, for a gateway, its signed receipt checked out). documented_policy: a no-retention policy the provider states, not proven by hardware. provider: may keep or log the prompt under its own terms. unproven_provider: an attested enclave was required or reported and not shown. unknown: the receipt does not say. none: served from the response cache, no provider ran.

reply_withheld.description: true when the router withheld the reply because the attested-enclave check failed; null when the receipt does not show which.

hidden.description: true only on the unlinkable lane.

stored.description: AnyRoute's software writes the client address to no table on current routes; null means handling is not established for an unfamiliar output type.

counter.description: Whether the address was the key of a rate-limit counter that expires about a minute later. Calls with an API key are limited per key (none); a call with no key is limited per address (about_a_minute); possible when the receipt does not say which.

identifies.description: What the receipt names as the payer: a key hash, a wallet address, or only the hash of a spent blind token.

fingerprints.description: SHA-256 fingerprints of the request and the reply are kept.

cache.description: The opt-in response cache holds an encrypted copy of the reply, never the prompt itself, until it expires; semantic caching also keeps a hashed word vector. Unrecognized content paths report eligibility as not_recorded. It is never used on the attested or unlinkable lanes or with a blind token; on the public lane only if the request asked for it.

tee.description: The TEE type from the router's attestation record for the receipt's attestation hash, when the receipt cites one; null when not known.

gpu_attested.description: true only when the gateway's signed receipt asserted GPU attestation.

development_report.description: true when the attestation behind the call was a development report, which is not a hardware proof.

summary.description: Three to five short lines a person who is not a developer can read.

short.description: The same in one line, for a chat message.

verify_url.description: The verify page for this receipt, when the router's address is known.

custom_id.description: Your id for the line, unique in the batch; results carry it back.

body.description: The chat completions or embeddings request body. stream true, model anyroute/council and verify are refused.

BatchCreateRequest.description: Send requests or input_jsonl. input_file_id is refused with 400 (there is no files endpoint).

input_jsonl.description: The lines as JSON Lines text: one BatchRequestLine object per line.

endpoint.description: When given, every line's url must match it.

id.description: batch_ followed by a random id.

endpoint.description: The endpoint of the lines, as sent or as the lines' url.

errors.description: Problems found in the batch as a whole, else null.

input_file_id.description: Always null: the lines are sent inline.

status.description: validating: accepted, waiting for the worker. completed, failed, expired and cancelled are final.

output_file_id.description: Always null: read the results at output_url.

error_file_id.description: Always null: read the errors at errors_url.

expires_at.description: When unfinished lines expire (the end of the completion window), unix seconds.

usd.description: What the answered lines cost so far, at the batch price.

discount_bps.description: The discount in basis points; 5000 is half the normal price.

list_usd.description: What the same lines would cost as normal calls.

results_expire_at.description: When the output and errors files are deleted, unix seconds; null until the batch finishes.

id.description: batch_req_ followed by a random id.

response.description: The response to the line; null for a line that never ran.

request_id.description: The generation id (and receipt id) of an answered line.

body.description: The normal response body (usage.cost and receipt included), or { error } for a failed line.

PresetDocument.description: A preset: the routing part of a saved route plus prompt-side defaults. The whole document is at most 64 KB as JSON.

models.description: Catalog model ids in fallback order; no @route/ or @preset/ entries.

provider.description: The same provider preferences as a saved route (SavedRouteConfig.provider), including lane (public|attested) and disclosure (none|policy|any), where the stricter of the preset and the request applies.

params.description: The same closed list of sampling defaults as a saved route (SavedRouteConfig.params). Request values win.

system_prompt.description: Prepended as a system message only when the request's messages have no system or developer message. Chat completions only.

response_format.description: text, json_object or json_schema (at most 16 KB). Used when the request sets no response_format.

tools.description: Function tool definitions (unique names, at most 32 KB). Used with tool_choice when the request sets no tools.

tool_choice.description: none, auto, required, or a function the preset's tools define.

model.description: Use as the request model, e.g. @preset/support; add @<version> to pin one.

version.description: The version shown: the latest unless one was asked for.

hash.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the version's canonical JSON. Equal content, equal hash.

versions.description: In the list: how many versions the preset has.

changed.description: PUT and rollback: false when the document equals the latest version, so no version was added.

restored_from.description: For a rollback: the version whose content it copied.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the preset document.

model_info.description: general.architecture, general.parameter_count where the name states it, and <family>.context_length.

model.description: A name from GET /ollama/api/tags. :latest names the model itself.

format.description: "json" for JSON mode, or a JSON schema for structured output (response_format).

options.description: temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, seed, stop, frequency_penalty and presence_penalty map directly; repeat_penalty to repetition_penalty; num_predict to max_tokens (-1 and -2 set no limit). Other options tune a local runtime and are named in X-Anyroute-Ignored.

think.description: false leaves the model's reasoning out of the reply.

keep_alive.description: Accepted and ignored; 0 with no messages or prompt answers done_reason unload.

provider.description: The router's provider preferences, as on chat completions, for example {"lane":"attested"}.

images.description: Base64 images (user messages); the media type is read from the bytes.

tool_name.description: On a tool message: the tool whose call it answers.

model.description: A name from GET /ollama/api/tags. :latest names the model itself.

format.description: "json" for JSON mode, or a JSON schema for structured output (response_format).

options.description: temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, seed, stop, frequency_penalty and presence_penalty map directly; repeat_penalty to repetition_penalty; num_predict to max_tokens (-1 and -2 set no limit). Other options tune a local runtime and are named in X-Anyroute-Ignored.

think.description: false leaves the model's reasoning out of the reply.

keep_alive.description: Accepted and ignored; 0 with no messages or prompt answers done_reason unload.

provider.description: The router's provider preferences, as on chat completions, for example {"lane":"attested"}.

context.description: Deprecated in Ollama; accepted and named in X-Anyroute-Ignored.

anyroute.description: On the closing object: the receipt and where the call was served.
On the closing object: the receipt and where the call was served.

TracingSettings.description: Where to send one span per public-lane call made with this key. Calls on the attested and unlinkable lanes are never exported. URLs must be public https:// addresses. The endpoint, headers and keys are encrypted at rest and never returned. A secret left out of a PATCH keeps the stored one when the type is unchanged.

type.description: otlp: OTLP/HTTP JSON to your collector. langfuse: Langfuse public ingestion API. helicone: Helicone custom log API.

endpoint.description: otlp: collector base URL; /v1/traces is appended unless present. No query string.

headers.description: otlp: headers sent with every export, e.g. x-honeycomb-team or Authorization. Write-only.

include_content.description: Also export the prompt messages and the completion text. Off unless set.

Tracing.description: A key's tracing destination as the API returns it: no URL path, header value or secret.

target.description: Scheme and host only, e.g. https://api.honeycomb.io/…

public_key_hint.description: langfuse: the public key's first and last characters.

status.description: This router process's export counters for the key (GET /api/v1/keys/{hash} and PATCH only). null before the first export.

dropped.description: Dropped because the queue was full or the circuit was open.

model.description: A catalogue model whose architecture.output_modalities include rerank (GET /api/v1/models?output_modalities=rerank), optionally with :nitro (fastest providers first) or :floor (cheapest first).

documents.description: Strings, or objects with a text. Sent to the provider as strings.

top_n.description: How many results to return, best first. Default: every document.

return_documents.description: Attach each result's document text (the text you sent).

index.description: Position of the document in the request.

relevance_score.description: The provider's score. The router checks it and never makes one up.

results.description: Best first, ties by index, at most top_n.

search_units.description: One query over up to 100 documents, each split into chunks of 500 tokens.

estimated.description: true when the provider did not report a quantity it is priced on and the router's estimate was billed.

meta.description: The billed search units where Cohere clients read them.

address.description: The bound wallet or Safe, lowercase.

budget_usd.description: Org budget: a cap on the sum of the limits of the team's keys.

allocated_usd.description: The limits of the team's enabled, unexpired keys, summed.

head.description: The chain's head hash (64 zeros when empty).

subject.description: A wallet address, or the first 16 characters of a passkey's credential id.

role.description: Agents are API keys (POST /api/v1/keys with role agent), not invited people. Only the owner invites an admin.

key.description: The issued key (same shape as GET /api/v1/key): it expires after 12 hours and has a limit of 0.

actor.description: key:<16 hex>, passkey:<member id> or wallet:<address>.

detail.description: A few fixed fields about the change (role, limit, lane, version, hash). Never prompt text.

hash.description: sha256(bytes(prev_hash) || utf8(canonical JSON of {team, seq, at, actor, action, target, detail})), keys sorted recursively.

root.description: RFC 6962 Merkle root over the raw 32-byte entry hashes of that UTC hour.

message.description: Sign with personal_sign (EOA) or through the Safe (EIP-1271).

publicKey.description: Passkey: WebAuthn options with base64url binary fields (PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions to join, PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions to sign in). Attestation is none; sign-in uses discoverable passkeys and lists no credentials.

status.description: suggested and dismissed are seen only by the operator.

evidence.description: Automatic suggestions only: lanes, surfaces, window (5m for the public lane, 1h for the private lanes), availability, target, requests and source (request-aggregates or dp-noised).

targets.description: Availability target per lane, as a fraction (STATUS_SLO_PUBLIC 0.995, STATUS_SLO_ATTESTED 0.99, STATUS_SLO_UNLINKABLE 0.99).

source.description: dp-noised: every figure is summed from the differentially private hourly releases, never from per-request records.

scope.description: Private lanes: attested+unlinkable, because the two lanes share one set of noisy counters.

windows.description: Per window (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d): availability (null without enough data), eligible requests (5xx and successes; 4xx and 429 are left out) and error counts by class.

latency_24h.description: p50_ms and p95_ms as the upper edge of the fixed latency bucket each falls in. Public lane: time to first token for streams, full response otherwise. Private lanes: total generation time, the only latency the noisy counters keep.

error_budget.description: Over 30 days: allowed_failures, failures, remaining (share of the budget unspent) and exhausted.

daily.description: 90 UTC days, oldest first: availability (null without data) and eligible requests.

privacy.description: Private lanes: mechanism, epsilon per hour, noise scale and the minimum noisy eligible count before a share is shown.

surfaces.description: Per API surface, public lane only. rerank appears only where the router serves it.

synthetic_24h.description: Provider probes and canaries over 24 hours.

CharacterCard.description: A Tavern character card in its canonical form. card_hash is the SHA-256 of this object as canonical JSON.

data.description: The card's fields as the Tavern character card V2 and V3 specs define them. A V1 card (flat fields) is read as V2. Fields the router does not use are kept as they are.

character_book.description: The lorebook: entries with keys and content.

model.description: The model id that calls this character: @character/<id>.

visibility.description: public: listed in discovery and readable by anyone. unlisted: readable by anyone with the id, not listed. private: sealed on the owner's device; only the owner can read it.

name.description: null for a private card: the router never sees it.

card_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical card JSON. For a private card the client computes it before sealing, and a chat call's decrypted card is checked against it.

default_model.description: The model that answers when a call names none (no models[0]).

sealed_card.description: Private cards, to the owner only: the card encrypted on the owner's device (arm1.<iv>.<ciphertext>). The router cannot read it.

owner.description: true when the calling key owns this card.

CharacterInput.description: Send the card as JSON (card) or as a PNG that carries it (png). A private card is sealed on the client instead: send sealed_card and card_hash, never the plaintext.

card.description: A Tavern character card: V1 (flat fields), V2 (chara_card_v2) or V3 (chara_card_v3) JSON.

png.description: A PNG, base64, that carries the card in a ccv3 or chara tEXt chunk (ccv3 wins when both are present).

sealed_card.description: Private only: the card encrypted on the client (sealCard in @anyroute/client/characters). The router stores it as it is and never sees the plaintext.

card_hash.description: Private only: the SHA-256 of the canonical card JSON, computed before sealing.

CharacterChatRequest.description: A chat completions request plus the character options. The character's prompt is built by the router from the card; lanes, budgets and receipts apply as on /chat/completions. model, when set, is the model that answers; otherwise models[0], then the card's default model.

session_id.description: Your own id for a conversation, so regenerate knows which turn to redo.

greeting.description: Which greeting opens the chat: 0 is first_mes, 1 and up are alternate_greetings.

regenerate.description: Answer the last user turn again.

memory.description: Memory the client decrypted from its ledger. Used for this call, in memory only, and never stored.

card.description: Private cards only: the card decrypted on the client. It must hash to the character's card_hash, or the call is refused.

members.description: The characters in the group chat, in order.

mode.description: round_robin: the next member after the last speaker. named: the member the last message names, else round robin.

messages.description: The chat so far, as chat completions messages; an assistant message's name is the character that spoke.

scope.description: Derived on the client: an HMAC of the character id under the viewing key, so the router cannot tell which character a memory belongs to.

sealed.description: arm1.<base64url iv>.<base64url ciphertext>, encrypted on the client. The router stores only this.

key_id.description: Which of the client's keys sealed it.

embedding_opt_in.description: Store the embedding for POST /api/v1/memory/search. Off by default: a vector is derived from the memory's text and can leak its topic.

sealed.description: Only when one entry is read (GET /api/v1/memory/{id}).

rule.description: Rule id, e.g. exfil.env_to_network, injection.override, obfuscation.base64_blob, shell.rm_root, deps.untrusted_index, binary.executable.

excerpt.description: Up to 160 characters of the line, with hidden characters shown escaped.

score.description: 100 minus a weight per distinct rule and file: low 3, medium 10, high 25, critical 50.

level.description: dangerous with any high or critical finding or a score under 40; caution with any medium finding or a score under 90; trusted otherwise.

content_hash.description: sha256 (hex) of the canonical tar of the skill's files.

chain.description: Arguments for SkillRegistry.publish(skillHash, author, priceUSDG, trustLevel, uri).

receipt.description: Ed25519 signature (receipt key) over the canonical JSON of payload.

prompt.description: Positive decimal USD per token, at most 1000000.

completion.description: Positive decimal USD per token, at most 1000000.

canonical.description: Exact UTF-8 canonical policy bytes: sorted object keys, retained array order, no whitespace or trailing newline.

value.description: Base64 detached Ed25519 signature over canonical UTF-8 bytes.

verifier_key.description: C2SP signed-note verifier key. Pin independently; this response alone does not authenticate the operator.

proof_url.description: Inclusion proof under a signed checkpoint; independent checkpoint checks are separate.
